# Gate files: the checks that judge a change.
#
# `.github/workflows/guards-from-base.yml` and
# `node scripts/review-triggers.mjs --gates` read this list from the BASE
# commit, never from the pull request, and name every listed file the pull
# request edits. A check the change can edit is a check it can switch off,
# so an edit here is reviewed on its own. REVIEW.md R38's trigger is this
# list (its `gate-files` keyword), so the two cannot drift.
#
# One glob per line (`**` spans folders, `{a,b}` alternates); `#` starts a
# comment. A line starting `run ` also has its base copy RUN against the
# pull request's code when the pull request edits it: a rule test whose
# base copy should still pass after any change that keeps to the rule (a
# scan for a banned call, a pinned workflow shape). If the base copy fails,
# the change loosened a rule its own code relies on, extended a list the
# test enumerates, or moved a helper the base's copy imports.
#
# Tests that pin BEHAVIOUR (the `.cross.test.ts` mirror pins) or ENUMERATE
# the codebase (`mirrorCrossTestGate`, `claudeMdFreshness`) change with the
# code they pin, so their base copies fail on ordinary changes. They are
# named, not run. So are the `functions/` guards: the root suite does not
# run `functions/`. Measured on main's history in docs/agents/review.md.

# The checklist, the standards it is mined from, and this list
REVIEW.md
CODING_STANDARDS.md
.github/gate-files.txt
scripts/review-triggers.mjs
run scripts/review-triggers.test.ts
